findings.title: $primary lightness changed from 30% to 70% (visual regression on light themes)
findings.body: The PR pattern is to preserve the $primary lightness and only add a $secondary variant for dark themes, e.g. `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` → `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. This line breaks that pattern: `.topic-meta-data h5 a` originally was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` (a very dark color used for bold inline links inside topic meta data on the topic page). After the change it becomes `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so on light themes the link is now a much lighter shade (lightness 70 instead of 30), making the bold link fade against light backgrounds — a clear visual regression. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name $primary lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Inside `.user-main .user-stream .group-member-info`, `.name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and was changed to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This makes the user's name lighter on light themes than before (30% → 50%) and no longer matches the sibling `.title` (also 50/50) — the original intent was clearly to keep `.name` darker than `.title`. Should mirror the value, e.g. `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: .group-member-info .name $primary lightness changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: Same bug as the desktop counterpart: `.group-member-info .name` originally `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. On mobile light themes, group-member names are now lighter than they were, diverging from `.title` which remains 50/50. Should preserve the 30% lightness for the light theme branch.

findings.title: .topic-map h3 $primary lightness changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The mobile `.topic-map h3` rule originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);` is converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/topic-post.scss` correctly keeps the 20% primary value (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`). On mobile light themes, this header is now significantly lighter (50% vs 20%), reducing contrast against the light topic-map background. Should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))` to match desktop behavior.

findings.title: .custom-message-length $primary lightness inverted (70% → 30%)
findings.body: `.custom-message-length` originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly preserves 70% for the primary branch (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`). On mobile light themes, the character-count hint becomes a very dark color (30%) instead of the original muted/lighter shade (70%), making it visually inconsistent with the desktop modal and harder to read as a hint. Should mirror the value rather than invert it: `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.
